notes.md: - **Ismail Adil Shah (Bijapur):** lost the **Battle of Raichur (1520)** to **Krishnadevaraya** of Vijayanagara, who then took the **Raichur fort**.

new.s: Which Sultan of Delhi followed the ulema and showed respect to the Egyptian Caliph?
new.x: Firoz Tughlaq ruled on theocratic lines, followed the ulema and respected the Egyptian Caliph.
new.angle: U0115 notes gap: Firoz -> Egyptian Caliph

new.s: In Qutb Shahi Golconda, what were the tax-farming rights given to Brahmins called?
new.x: Golconda gave Brahmins agraharas and Mustajir (tax-farming) rights.
new.angle: U0115 notes gap: Brahmins -> Mustajir rights

new.s: Who was Lal Ded?
new.x: Lal Ded was a Kashmiri saint; she never ruled Delhi.
new.angle: U0115 notes gap: Lal Ded = Kashmir saint

new.s: Who built the Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal) at Mehrauli?
new.x: Balban built the Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal) and his own tomb at Mehrauli.
new.angle: U0116 notes gap: Red Palace -> Balban

new.s: Who added a madrasa and his own tomb at Hauz Khas, on the tank of Alauddin Khalji?
new.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq built a madrasa and his tomb at Hauz Khas beside Alauddin's tank.
new.angle: U0116 notes gap: Hauz Khas madrasa -> Firoz

new.s: In which citadel of Delhi stands the Ashokan pillar brought from Topra?
new.x: Firoz Shah Kotla, the citadel of Firozabad, holds the Topra Ashokan pillar.
new.angle: U0116 notes gap: Topra pillar -> Firoz Shah Kotla

new.s: During whose reign was the Moth ki Masjid in Delhi built?
new.x: The Moth ki Masjid was built in Sikandar Lodi's reign, in the Lodi style.
new.angle: U0116 notes gap: Moth ki Masjid -> Sikandar Lodi

new.s: Who built the Kirti Stambha at Chittor?
new.x: The Kirti Stambha at Chittor is credited to Rana Kumbha of Mewar.
new.angle: U0116 notes gap: Kirti Stambha -> Rana Kumbha

new.s: After which Sufi saint is the Qutb Minar commonly believed to be named?
new.x: The Qutb Minar is commonly believed to be named after Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (the point is debated).
new.angle: U0116 notes gap: Qutb Minar name -> Bakhtiyar Kaki

new.s: Which of the following is regarded as the earliest Shiva Linga?
new.x: The Gudimallam Shiva Linga (Andhra Pradesh) is regarded as the earliest Shiva Linga.
new.angle: U0116 notes gap: earliest Shiva Linga -> Gudimallam

new.s: Who is the author of Tarikh-i-Ferishta, also called Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi?
new.x: Tarikh-i-Ferishta (Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi) was written by Muhammad Qasim Ferishta.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Tarikh-i-Ferishta -> author

new.s: At the court of which ruler did Ferishta write his history?
o: Ahmad Shah I of the Bahmanis
Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda
new.x: Ferishta wrote at Bijapur under Ibrahim Adil Shah, naming the work Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi after him.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Ferishta -> patron Ibrahim Adil Shah

new.s: Where was the historian Ferishta born?
new.x: Ferishta was born at Astarabad in 1552.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Ferishta -> birthplace

new.s: In which year did Ibn Battuta come to Delhi?
new.x: Ibn Battuta reached Delhi in 1333 and stayed in India till 1342.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Ibn Battuta -> year of arrival

new.s: At which place was Ibn Battuta born?
new.x: Ibn Battuta was born at Tangiers in Morocco in 1304.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Ibn Battuta -> Tangiers

new.s: What was the real name of Amir Khusrau?
new.x: Amir Khusrau's real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau; he was born at Patiyali.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Khusrau -> real name

new.s: Which work of Amir Khusrau describes the rise of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq?
new.x: Khusrau's Tughluqnama deals with the rise of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Tughluqnama -> subject

new.s: Who among the following is credited with starting the qaul and tarana forms of music?
new.x: Amir Khusrau is credited with qawwali and with starting qaul, qalbana, tarana and khayal.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Khusrau -> qaul, tarana

new.s: What is the Razmnama?
o: Persian translation of the Suka Saptati
new.x: The Razmnama is the Persian Mahabharata of the Mughal period.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Razmnama -> Persian Mahabharata

new.s: Kalila wa Dimna is the Persian version of which work?
new.x: Kalila wa Dimna is the Persian Panchatantra.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Kalila wa Dimna -> Panchatantra

new.s: Who wrote the Nirvachanottara Ramayanam?
new.x: Tikkana of the Kakatiya period wrote Nirvachanottara Ramayanam and 15 parvas of the Mahabharata.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Nirvachanottara Ramayanam -> Tikkana

new.s: Who is the author of Sringara Naishadham?
new.x: Srinatha of the Reddi period wrote Sringara Naishadham and Kasi Khandam.
new.angle: U0117 notes gap: Sringara Naishadham -> Srinatha

new.s: Who founded the independent Sultanate of Gujarat in 1407?
new.x: Zafar Khan, as Muzaffar Shah I, founded the Gujarat Sultanate in 1407.
new.angle: U0118 notes gap: Gujarat -> founder

new.s: Who founded the independent Sultanate of Malwa in 1401?
new.x: Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401 and founded the Malwa Sultanate.
new.angle: U0118 notes gap: Malwa -> founder

new.s: What was the original name of Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir?
new.x: Zain-ul-Abidin was originally named Shahi Khan; he was the brother of Ali Shah.
new.angle: U0118 notes gap: Zain-ul-Abidin -> original name

new.s: Who continued Kalhana's Rajatarangini in the time of Zain-ul-Abidin?
new.x: Jonaraja continued the Rajatarangini under Zain-ul-Abidin.
new.angle: U0118 notes gap: Rajatarangini continued -> Jonaraja

new.s: After which Sultan was the city of Jaunpur named?
new.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq founded Jaunpur and named it after Muhammad bin Tughlaq (Jauna Khan).
new.angle: U0118 notes gap: Jaunpur -> named after

new.s: Mahmud Begarha of Gujarat joined which power against the Portuguese?
new.x: Mahmud Begarha joined Egypt against the Portuguese: they won at Chaul (1508) but lost at Diu (1509).
new.angle: U0118 notes gap: Mahmud Begarha -> Egypt vs Portuguese

new.s: What was the capital of the Faruqi kingdom of Khandesh?
new.x: The Faruqis of Khandesh, founded by Malik Raja Faruqi (1382), ruled from Burhanpur.
new.angle: U0118 notes gap: Faruqi -> capital

new.s: Who founded Bikaner?
new.x: Rao Bika of the Rathores founded Bikaner; Rao Jodha founded Jodhpur.
new.angle: U0118 notes gap: Bikaner -> Rao Bika

new.s: Which fort was built by Rana Kumbha of Mewar?
new.x: Rana Kumbha, a Sisodia of Mewar, built Kumbhalgarh and the Vijay Stambha.
new.angle: U0118 notes gap: Rana Kumbha -> Kumbhalgarh

new.s: Which was the first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan?
new.x: The Bahmani kingdom, founded in 1347, was the first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan.
new.angle: U0118 notes gap: first Muslim kingdom of Deccan -> Bahmani

new.s: Who were the Kayasthas in the Qutb Shahi administration?
new.x: In the Qutb Shahi administration the Kayasthas were scribes.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Kayastha -> scribes (APPSC G2 2012)

new.s: Which group worked as scribes in the Qutb Shahi administration?
new.x: Kayasthas were the scribes; Mustajirs were tax farmers and Mahasibs looked after public morals.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Kayastha -> scribes, other direction

new.s: Who headed a Pargana in the Qutb Shahi administration?
new.x: A Pargana was under a Tahsildar or Deshmukh; a Sarkar was under a Faujdar.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Pargana -> head

new.s: Who was the head of a village under the Qutb Shahis?
new.x: The Mukaddam was the village head; the Kulkarni was the village accountant.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: village -> Mukaddam

new.s: From which Turkmen tribe did the Qutb Shahis of Golconda come?
new.x: The Shia Qutb Shahis were Qara Qoyunlu (Black Sheep) Turkmen from Hamadan.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Qutb Shahi origin -> Qara Qoyunlu

new.s: In whose reign was the Hussain Sagar built in 1562?
new.x: The Hussain Sagar was built in 1562 under Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Hussain Sagar -> Ibrahim

new.s: After whom is the Hussain Sagar in Hyderabad named?
new.x: The Hussain Sagar is named after Hussain Shah Wali.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Hussain Sagar -> named after

new.s: At which court did Ibrahim Qutb Shah spend seven years in exile before his accession?
new.x: Ibrahim Qutb Shah spent seven years in exile at Vijayanagara.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Ibrahim -> exile at Vijayanagara

new.s: Which Qutb Shahi ruler governed along with his mother Hayat Bakshi Begum?
new.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah ruled with his mother Hayat Bakshi Begum.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Abdullah -> Hayat Bakshi Begum

new.s: Who built the Golconda Jama Masjid?
new.x: Sultan Quli strengthened Golconda fort and built the Golconda Jama Masjid.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Golconda Jama Masjid -> Sultan Quli

new.s: Which port in the Godavari delta was the chief shipbuilding port of the Golconda kingdom?
new.x: Narsapuram was the chief shipbuilding port; Machilipatnam was mainly a trade port.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: shipbuilding port -> Narsapuram

new.s: In which year was the Kohinoor diamond found?
new.x: The Kohinoor was found in 1656 in the Kollur mines.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Kohinoor -> year found

new.s: Which Portuguese traveller of the early 16th century described the diamond trade of the Golconda region?
new.x: Duarte Barbosa (Portuguese) described the diamond trade; Tavernier, a Frenchman, later gave the fullest account.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: diamond trade -> Duarte Barbosa

new.s: What is the weight of the Golconda Blue diamond that was in the news in May 2025?
new.x: The Golconda Blue is a 23.24-carat fancy vivid blue, pear-shaped diamond.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Golconda Blue -> 23.24 ct

new.s: Chand Sultana, the wife of Ibrahim Adil Shah II, was the sister of which ruler?
new.x: Ibrahim Adil Shah II married Chand Sultana, the sister of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Chand Sultana -> sister of Muhammad Quli

new.s: Against whom did Chand Bibi defend Ahmadnagar in 1595-96?
new.x: Chand Bibi defended Ahmadnagar against the Mughals in 1595-96 and died when it fell in 1600.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Chand Bibi -> defence against Mughals

new.s: Who set up Murtaza Nizam Shah III as a puppet Nizam Shahi ruler in 1634?
new.x: After 1633 Shahji Bhonsle set up Murtaza Nizam Shah III and held out till 1636.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Shahji Bhonsle -> puppet Nizam Shah

new.s: Where was Abul Hasan Tana Shah kept as a prisoner until his death in 1699?
new.x: Abul Hasan was imprisoned at Bidar and then Daulatabad; he died in 1699 and was buried at Khuldabad.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Abul Hasan -> imprisoned at Daulatabad

new.s: For how much a year was Machilipatnam leased under the Qutb Shahi revenue-farming system?
new.x: Machilipatnam was farmed out for 1,80,000 pagodas a year, an example of Qutb Shahi revenue farming.
new.angle: U0119 notes gap: Machilipatnam lease -> 1,80,000 pagodas

new.s: Which ruler of Bijapur lost the Battle of Raichur (1520) to Krishnadevaraya?
new.x: Krishnadevaraya defeated Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur at Raichur in 1520 and took the Raichur fort.
new.angle: U0119 web: PYQ y9d4eb959b30 Battle of Raichur -> Ismail Adil Shah

new.s: In the Battle of Raichur (1520), Krishnadevaraya defeated the forces of which Sultanate?
new.x: At Raichur (1520) Krishnadevaraya routed Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur.
new.angle: U0119 web: Battle of Raichur -> Bijapur

new.s: Which historian supported the Andhra origin theory of Harihara and Bukka?
new.x: The Andhra theory is backed by N. Venkataramanaiah, Sewell and Nilakanta Sastri; Heras, Rice and Ayyangar back the Kannada theory.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Andhra theory -> backers

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the origin of Harihara and Bukka:
1. Nilakanta Sastri supported the Andhra theory.
2. Father Heras supported the Andhra theory.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Nilakanta Sastri backed the Andhra theory; Father Heras backed the Kannada (Hoysala) theory.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Andhra vs Kannada theory -> backers

new.s: By which year was the city of Vijayanagara completed?
new.x: Founded in 1336, the city of Vijayanagara was completed by 1343.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: city completed -> 1343

new.s: Who among the following were the queens of Krishnadevaraya?
o: Hayat Bakshi Begum and Tirumala Devi
new.x: Krishnadevaraya's queens were Tirumala Devi and Chinna Devi; Nagala Devi was his mother.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Krishnadevaraya -> queens

new.s: Who was the father of Vira Narasimha, the founder of the Tuluva dynasty?
new.x: Tuluva Narasa Nayaka was the father of Vira Narasimha, who was crowned in 1505.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Vira Narasimha -> father

new.s: The Aravidu dynasty came from Araviti, in which present district of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: The Aravidu dynasty, of Andhra origin, came from Araviti in Kurnool.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Aravidu -> Araviti, Kurnool

new.s: Which saint-composer was a contemporary of Krishnadevaraya?
new.x: Purandara Dasa (1484-1564) was a contemporary of Krishnadevaraya (1509-29); Annamacharya died in 1503.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Krishnadevaraya -> Purandara Dasa

new.s: During whose reign did the Portuguese Fernao Nuniz visit Vijayanagara?
new.x: Nuniz visited in the reign of Achyutaraya; Paes came under Krishnadevaraya.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Nuniz -> Achyutaraya

new.s: During whose reign did Domingo Paes visit Vijayanagara?
new.x: Domingo Paes, like Barbosa, visited during Krishnadevaraya's reign.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Paes -> Krishnadevaraya

new.s: Which Sangama ruler's forces took Goa and Belgaum in 1380?
new.x: Goa and Belgaum were taken in 1380 under Harihara II.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Goa, Belgaum 1380 -> Harihara II

new.s: Which work was written by Irugappa, the minister of Harihara II?
new.x: Irugappa built the Ganigitti Jain temple and wrote Navaratnamala.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Irugappa -> Navaratnamala

new.s: Whom did Kumara Kampana overthrow in his southern campaign before destroying the Madurai Sultanate?
new.x: Kumara Kampana, son of Bukka I, overthrew Sambhuvaraya and then destroyed the Madurai Sultanate.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Kampana -> Sambhuvaraya

new.s: Whom did Srinatha defeat in debate at the court of Devaraya II?
new.x: Srinatha defeated Dindima Bhatta and received a kanakabhishekam from Devaraya II.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Srinatha -> Dindima Bhatta

new.s: Who held the title 'Dakshina Samudradhipati'?
new.x: Dakshina Samudradhipati was the title of Lakkanna Dandanayaka; Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati was Harihara I's.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Dakshina Samudradhipati -> Lakkanna

new.s: Gangadevi, the author of Madhura Vijayam, was a disciple of whom?
new.x: Gangadevi, wife of Kumara Kampana, was a disciple of Agastya.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Gangadevi -> guru

new.s: Besides Jaimini Bharatam, which work did Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadrudu write?
new.x: Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadrudu wrote Jaimini Bharatam and Sringara Sakuntalam in the Saluva era.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Pinaveerabhadrudu -> Sringara Sakuntalam

new.s: Which city does Vinukonda Vallabharaya's Kridabhiramam describe?
new.x: Kridabhiramam describes Kakatiya Warangal.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Kridabhiramam -> Warangal

new.s: Against whom did Devaraya I fight in coastal Andhra?
new.x: Devaraya I fought the Kandukuru Reddis and allied with the Velamas and Kataya Vema.
new.angle: U0120 notes gap: Devaraya I -> Kandukuru Reddis
